titulo: 4th Grade Science Practice for the Partial Exam

parte1.pregunta: Which of the following is a renewable resource?

opciones: It can be replaced and causes less pollution
It never runs out of oil
Gases that trap heat and make Earth warmer

parte1.pregunta: What do scrubbers do in power plants?
opciones: Clean dirty air before it goes outside

parte1.pregunta: Which energy source does not create smoke but produces hot water waste?
What can happen if oil spills into the ocean?
opciones: Animals can be hurt or die

parte1.pregunta: How do we move fuels like oil and gas?
Which is a clean energy technology that helps the environment?
Why is it better to use renewable energy like solar and wind?
What can happen when fuel is transported?
opciones: They can spill and pollute land and water

parte2.rubrica: Full credit: a resource/energy that can be replaced (renewed) naturally or quickly, so it does not run out as we use it. 1 point for 'can be replaced/renewed', 1 point for 'does not run out'. Optional extra idea: causes less pollution.
1 point for each correct type, up to 2: solar, wind, hydropower (moving/flowing water, hydroelectric), geothermal, biomass. Coal, oil, natural gas and nuclear are NOT renewable (0 for those).

parte2.pregunta: How does burning fuels affect the air?
parte2.rubrica: 1 point: it pollutes the air / releases smoke, ash, pollutants or harmful chemicals. 1 point: it releases greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (trap heat, warm the Earth) OR chemicals that cause acid rain.
1 point: they clean the gases / reduce the pollutants (dirty air). 1 point: they do it in power plants before the gases go into the air (outside).

1 point: energy produced in nuclear power plants from atoms (splitting atoms of uranium / energy stored in the nucleus). 1 point: a characteristic from the book: it does not produce smoke or air pollutants, BUT it produces dangerous solid waste and lots of hot water. A child who says 'energy from nuclear power plants that does not make smoke but produces hot water waste' gets full credit.

parte2.pregunta: How does mining and drilling harm the environment?
parte2.rubrica: 1 point: mining/drilling changes or damages the land: forests and fields are removed, habitats are lost, roads break up habitats. 1 point: pollution: mined materials dissolve and pollute streams and rivers; drilling uses toxic materials that can spill and pollute land and water.

parte2.pregunta: What can happen to animals during oil spills?
parte2.rubrica: 1 point: the sticky oil covers them / gets on their feathers or fur / they swallow it. 1 point: they can get hurt, sick, cannot fly or swim, or die; their habitat is polluted.

1 point: names a technology: scrubbers, electric cars, solar panels, wind turbines, cleaner machines. 1 point: explains how it helps (cleans gases before they reach the air; uses electricity/sun/wind instead of burning fuel, so no smoke or greenhouse gases).

parte3.descripcion: Energy that comes from the Sun.
A special machine that cleans dirty air.
Energy from the inside of the Earth.
Energy made from plants and animal waste.
Harmful gases or waste in the environment.
Energy doesn't make smoke but produces hot water waste.

parte4.pregunta: Explain why renewable resources are better for the environment than burning fuels. Include at least two examples.
parte4.rubrica: 1 point: renewable resources do not run out / can be replaced. 1 point: they cause less pollution: no burning, little or no smoke or greenhouse gases (burning fuels pollutes the air). 1 point: at least two correct examples (solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, biomass). 1 point: well-organized paragraph with complete sentences and key vocabulary.

parte4.pregunta: Describe some ways energy use can harm the environment. Mention pollution, mining, drilling, or oil spills.
parte4.rubrica: Up to 3 points, 1 for each harm correctly explained: air pollution from burning fuels (smoke, greenhouse gases, acid rain); mining (forests removed, habitat loss, polluted rivers); drilling (roads, cut forests, toxic materials spill); oil spills (sticky oil hurts animals, spreads on water); hot water from power plants; nuclear waste. 1 point: well-organized paragraph with complete sentences and key vocabulary.

parte4.pregunta: Explain how technology can help reduce pollution and protect the Earth. Include examples like scrubbers, electric cars, or solar panels.
parte4.rubrica: 1 point: explains that technology can reduce pollution (cleaner energy, less burning of fuels). 1 point: scrubbers clean gases/dirty air before it goes outside. 1 point: electric cars (no gasoline, no exhaust smoke) or solar panels/wind turbines (electricity without burning fuel). 1 point: well-organized paragraph with complete sentences and key vocabulary.
